chunks: From him, from his father, raising it to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
No deed with doubt and denial will be of any benefit.

key_terms.الشَّكِّ: Doubt, uncertainty regarding the validity or obligation of an act
key_terms.الْجُحُودِ: Denial, refusal to accept or acknowledge the truth or requirement
key_terms.عَمَلٌ: Deed, action, or act of worship

ai.seo_question: What conditions make a religious deed beneficial or ineffective according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS), emphasizing that internal conviction is the prerequisite for the acceptance of external actions. Shia scholars highlight that 'denial' (juhud) here refers not just to disbelief, but to a lack of sincere certainty in the act's validity, rendering the deed spiritually void despite its outward correctness. This underscores the principle that the heart's state determines the worth of the body's movements in worship.
